Klawer Murder

By: Floris Kotze | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
SA is gripped with yet another alleged occult murder, this time, in a small picturesque town of Klawer. Traumatised locals blame police for failing them. We visit Klawer to find the truth.

Unique Selling Point:
Early in February 2022, a man from a small town in the Western Cape’s Olifants Valley was arrested for the murder of 13-year-old Jerobejin van Wyk. Daniel Smit (56) has told his lawyer his actions were part of occult killings he had practiced since childhood. Smit has been charged with murder, kidnapping, assault with intent to cause grievous bodily harm, and defeating the ends of justice. But is there more to this crime?

Summary:
Rumours are rife in the town as to what exactly happened when Jerobejin disappeared, Wednesday the 2nd of February.
5 children were allegedly talking to Daniel Smit, shortly before the incident. Photos have emerged of this interaction, but I am unable to prove authenticity of the photos. In the photos, Smit seems relaxed. Talking to the kids, counting down with his fingers closing in his left hand palm.
As if they have had plenty of conversations with the boys before.

But the situation would soon take a turn for the worse.
Something happened. But what?




Further information:
The kids ran away from his house.
Smit got in his bakkie and followed them.

In an effort to hide from Smit, one of Jerobejin’s friends hid in a dustbin, whilst Jerobejin kept running.
Smit allegedly hit Jerobejin and drove over him. Breaking his neck. Smit got out, picked him up, and put him in the back of the bakkie. And drove off.

This whole incident was being observed by a man filling up at a petrol station nearby, a witness. He is also willing speak to us, anonymously. He says no SAPS member approached or requested information from him, regarding that dreadful day.
The witness could not believe his eyes.

Jerobejin was now missing.

Jerobejin’s mother, Triesa Van Wyk, went to the Klawer Police Station and two officers accompanied her to the house of Smit.
“I looked him in the face and asked him where is my son, and he told me he took my child to buy him food but when he came out of the shop, he was gone.”
This was a blatant lie, as Smit later admitted.
Police only arrested Smit on Thursday. Police and forensics searched his property.
On Friday they found body parts, stuffed in a drain outside the house. Police took DNA from Van Wyk, and is currently being analysed. We do not yet know the DNA results. Triesa, Jerobejin’s mother, however, is convinced it is her boy’s remains.


“A mother just knows” a tearful Triesa told the media.

It has since emerged that Smit took the body of Jerobejin, butchered it and tried to dispose of it. Allegedly, all part of an occult “sacrifice”, he told his lawyer Santie Human. She confirmed she will do an interview. Providing that it won’t interfere with the case.

The Satanists’ Group has since denied that Smit is a member. Nor any affiliation.

Some community members believe the murder was not an occult killing but rather racially motivated. This is the crux of the matter as the “dorpie” is very much divided at the moment. This is, unfortunately, not the first time children disappeared from this area. Over the last 3 years, 3 teenagers disappeared. Including a disabled child. With all the anger in the commity, is it reasonable for the community to want to blame Smit for these incidents too?
Klawer community activist Billy Claasen, confirmed that some children were never found. He also added that this was not a crime linked to colour or race.
“It is one sick White man that did this, so it could have been a sick Coloured or Black man who could have done it."

Claasen is also willing to do an interview. Admitting that the tension this created, has never been experienced by the townspeople.

Unfortunately, more disturbing news for Klawer.

Another murder.

Allegedly, racially motivated.
This occurred Saturday the 12th of February.
A coloured man stabbed and killed an African man. He was murdered after midnight. Unrest prevented the ambulance to get to the scene. The body was eventually removed around 06:00 in the morning.


Local councilman Jan Koopman is convinced, if the police acted sooner in arresting Smit, the current situation in Klawer could have been avoided. The community is calling for Klawer SAPS Station commander, Captain Ficks, to resign. Cllr Koopman says the community lost confidence in the SAPS. A long time ago.

I approached the Western Cape Police Spokesperson, Colonel André Traut, he will answer to some questions, providing I send it to him prior to filming. I will most certainly put a question to him regarding Klawer SAPS.

Cllr Koopman, also acting as the spokesperson for the Van Wyk’s family, assured me that Triesa van Wyk, Jerobejin’s mother will talk to us.
Van Wyk was not allowed in court when Smit appeared on Monday the 7th of February. This was despite the community protesting outside the court, to allow her access.
Meanwhile, Smit stated that he will plead guilty, but even more shockingly, other murders too. Allegedly as part of the “occult”.

Human, his lawyer, stated that Smit is fully co-operative. He is helping the police in finding “whatever evidence they need, where to find certain objects, like knives and tools he used to butcher the boy.”

“He is divulging, whatever evidence, the investigating officers require of him.” she told me off the record.


SAPS is currently investigating and looking into linking other murders to him,
this in an effort to charge him once, and bring all murder charges to court.
“He denies any involvement in the other missing children from Klawer” according to Human.
She also added, “he is not pure evil.”


Smit’s next court appearance will be 26th of April.

Script:


Klawer Mystery (Scripted Text)

SCRAMBLED AUDIO: “A Klawer man has been arrested for the murder of a missing 13 year old boy…”
“Police found human remains in sewage pipes at a man’s home on Friday…”

LINK: This is the small town of Klawer, named after the clover. It’s about a 3 hour’s drive north of Cape Town and surrounded by beautiful mountain ranges. It is known for its grapes it’s rooibos it's honey and citrus, it’s also called a ‘little corridor of unusualness’ which takes on a rather sinister light in view of recent events.


VO:
In this scenic little town, situated on the cusp of the Western and Northern Cape, a truly disturbing murder occured.
Jerobejin van Wyk, a 13 year-old boy was killed then butchered in this house. It sparked racial tension and caused uproar in the community.
Daniel Smit, has admitted to killing Jerobejin. He has been described by many as a quiet individual, but, also, a man with a troubling past.

Tries:
I would like to ask him, what my child's final words were?
That is what I'd really would like to know.
He must tell me!

VO:
Triesa van Wyk, the mother of murdered Jerobejin, has been searching for answers ever since he disappeared on the 2nd of February.

Tries:
How could he butcher a child like that?

Santie:
He was in the occult since the age of 13 for 20 years. He was not a satanist although he did make a contract with Satan and the cult group, he says there were two contracts he made, in blood.

VO:
Santie Human has been a lawyer in the district of Matzikama for over 20 years. Smit approached her when the police questioned him about the missing child, Jerobejin. She is representing him in his upcoming trial. He has given her explicit instructions to answer the questions Carte Blanche posed, as long as the case is not jeopardised.

Derek:
What do you think made Daniel angry at the house when Jerobejin and his friends were hanging around?
Santie:
A lot of the people living in Klawer are frustrated with young kids coming into their houses and stealing stuff, so the frustration I think, got to him that day. He wanted to ask them, “what were you doing in my yard?''





Deeno (Jerobejin’s Friend):
We were looking for cans. We go through the trash, looking for cans
and then we sell it.

VO:
This is Jerobejin’s friend “Deeno”. He was with Jerobejin on that fateful day, when they noticed some fruit on Smit’s property.

Deeno (Jerobejin’s Friend):
We climbed over the wall, a small wall. As we were climbing over the wall
Daniel shouted:
"If I catch you, you will never see your parents again."
That was all he said.

VO:
The boys scattered and ran away from Smit’s house. He got in his vehicle and gave chase. The boys were hiding behind houses, buildings and even the cemetery. Still, Smit followed them.

Santie:
That is when the occult resorts back into him. So he felt out of control and tried to be in control.

Dino
We saw him racing towards us in his bakkie. That's when I jumped into a bin.

VO:
Whilst Deeno was hiding in this bin, Jerobejin decided to get away on his own.
Watch this exclusive CCTV footage of Smit trying to corner Jerobejin.

Deeno:
Jerobejin still yelled at me, saying I must run! I heard a thud. I never saw him again. I never heard from him again.

LINK:
That thud was apparently Smit's bakkie colliding with Jerobejin right here, apparently he was still alive, trying to sit up, when Smith threw him into the back of the vehicle and tore off.

Triesa
When I got home that evening, I then went to the police station.
They kept me there the whole evening.

VO:
A service delivery complaint, including not taking the missing persons report seriously, was lodged against Klawer Police.
This, after Triesa, allegedly, had to wait several hours for an Afrikaans speaking officer to assist her.






Triesa:
How can they have two black officers at the station? Knowing that when a coloured person arrives they won't be able to understand the language.

Col Traut:
The allegations made that there was no Afrikaans speaking police officer on duty to interview to Jerobejin's mother was investigated and it was found that there was no basis for such a complaint

VO:
The Western Cape Police spokesperson Colonel André Traut, informed us that an internal investigation was launched to look into the complaints.

Col: Andre Traut
The allegation that the missing person’s report was not taken seriously, has been refuted by our internal investigation. It was found that police officers were immediately deployed in the area to start the search for the missing boy.

VO:
Triesa was sent home from the police station at around 03:00, Thursday morning, without any answers. She knew Jerobejin had been taken by Smit, but the thought of murder did not cross her mind.

Derek:
Did he say that Jerobejin was still alive?
Santie:
It is definitely so that he was still alive. And when he came to the house, the daughter also saw him walking. So he was definitely alive.
Derek:
So what happened at the house?
Santie:
There things went wrong. There things went wrong. I will not really go into that in detail at this stage. But there he made the decision and he killed the boy.
Derek:
How did he kill him?
Santie:
He broke his neck.
Derek:
Broke his neck?
Santie:
I don’t want to say how.
Not at this stage.

Link:
Santie is now gonna take us into Daniel Smith's house, which I am feeling a little bit nervous about…

Santie:
This is where they came through.
Derek:
The garage?
Santie:
Ja the garage, Daniel and the boy they walked in here and walked to the kitchen.
Daniel gave Jerobejin a piece of bread to eat and something to drink, and that is when he broke his neck.
VO:
Smit then put the body in a chest freezer until the evening.

Santie:
There was body parts that showed that it was based in a fireplace and that is the truth and I can show you the fire place.
Derek:
What, put his body, or parts of his body in here?
Santie:
Yes
Derek:
Do you think Daniel is happy with us knowing about this?
Santie:
Daniel wants the truth to be told, because people are still looking for the body and looking for something more to bury there's nothing more. There’s nothing more.
Derek:
This is it.
Santie:
This is it.
Derek:
Burnt here, the rest in the drain.

VO:
A local municipal worker noticed Smit was tampering with the drains, the day after Jerobejin disappeared.
This was peculiar behaviour as the municipality services the drains regularly.

Billy:
The municipal workers were busy pumping the drain when something blocked the pipe.
And then they pull out, with a piece of wire, pulled out pieces of meat. It was this part, and then the hair, and a piece of one ear.

VO:
Billy Klaasen is a former farmworker turned activist. He started the Rural and Farmworkers' Development Organisation to help marginalised labourers. He was called in to assist when Jerobejin was reported as missing.

I said, I told you guys, this is the child and then, swearing at this captain
“Get up from your *ss!” and phone the people to come, and then they took over the scene again, as a crime scene.

VO:
DNA tests confirmed that it was Jerobejin. Smit was already detained for kidnapping and is now facing charges of Murder, Kidnapping, Assault and obstructing the ends of justice.
The next court date is set for the 26th of April.
Even though Triesa is still grieving, she will attend the hearing, hoping to find more answers.

Triesa:
I woke up last night and was about 12, then I came to sit with my child and cry by my child. Just to think how he called me, his Mom, while that man was busy with him, he called me and that's what hurts my heart so much. I was not there to help.
I will never forgive him, I will never forgive him.
VO:
Since Jerobejin’s murder, community improvement projects have been started in an attempt to keep children off the streets.
The death of Jerobejin shocked the whole town, and like Triesa, residents are desperate for answers.
They have stood strong by her side from the very beginning.
And as Triesa wait for the trial to commence,
perhaps, now, Jerobejin is the one person that can unite the town of Klawer.


11’
South Africa is rocked by yet another alleged occult murder. This time in the small picturesque town of Klawer. We go in search of the truth

21”
We enter the house of the alleged occult killer from Klawer in the Western Cape, uncovering the truth about the brutal death of a 13 year old boy.
Santie: This is the Kitchen where he made him a sandwich.
We uncover the disturbing details of the murder.


21”
We travel to Klawer in the Western Cape and speak to the mother of murdered Jerobejin van Wyk.
Tries:
I want to know the whole truth. What happened to my son? What did he do to my son?
What was his last words?
We uncover disturbing details of yet another alleged occult killing.

Santie: A lot of the people living in Klawer are frustrated with young kids coming into their houses and stealing stuff, so the frustration I think, got to him that day. He wanted to ask them, “what were you doing in my yard?'' Deeno (Jerobejin’s Friend): We were looking for cans. We go through the trash, looking for cans and then we sell it. VO: This is Jerobejin’s friend “Deeno”. He was with Jerobejin on that fateful day, when they noticed some fruit on Smit’s property. Deeno (Jerobejin’s Friend): We climbed over the wall, a small wall. As we were climbing over the wall Daniel shouted: "If I catch you, you will never see your parents again." That was all he said. VO: The boys scattered and ran away from Smit’s house. He got in his vehicle and gave chase. The boys were hiding behind houses, buildings and even the cemetery. Still, Smit followed them. Santie: That is when the occult resorts back into him. So he felt out of control and tried to be in control. Dino We saw him racing towards us in his bakkie. That's when I jumped into a bin. VO: Whilst Deeno was hiding in this bin, Jerobejin decided to get away on his own. Watch this exclusive CCTV footage of Smit trying to corner Jerobejin. Deeno: Jerobejin still yelled at me, saying I must run! I heard a thud. I never saw him again. I never heard from him again. LINK: That thud was apparently Smit's bakkie colliding with Jerobejin right here, apparently he was still alive, trying to sit up, when Smith threw him into the back of the vehicle and tore off. Triesa When I got home that evening, I then went to the police station. They kept me there the whole evening. VO: A service delivery complaint, including not taking the missing persons report seriously, was lodged against Klawer Police. This, after Triesa, allegedly, had to wait several hours for an Afrikaans speaking officer to assist her. Triesa: How can they have two black officers at the station? Knowing that when a coloured person arrives they won't be able to understand the language. Col Traut: The allegations made that there was no Afrikaans speaking police officer on duty to interview to Jerobejin's mother was investigated and it was found that there was no basis for such a complaint VO: The Western Cape Police spokesperson Colonel André Traut, informed us that an internal investigation was launched to look into the complaints. Col: Andre Traut The allegation that the missing person’s report was not taken seriously, has been refuted by our internal investigation. It was found that police officers were immediately deployed in the area to start the search for the missing boy. VO: Triesa was sent home from the police station at around 03:00, Thursday morning, without any answers. She knew Jerobejin had been taken by Smit, but the thought of murder did not cross her mind. Derek: Did he say that Jerobejin was still alive? Santie: It is definitely so that he was still alive. And when he came to the house, the daughter also saw him walking. So he was definitely alive. Derek: So what happened at the house? Santie: There things went wrong. There things went wrong. I will not really go into that in detail at this stage. But there he made the decision and he killed the boy. Derek: How did he kill him? Santie: He broke his neck. Derek: Broke his neck? Santie: I don’t want to say how. Not at this stage. Link: Santie is now gonna take us into Daniel Smith's house, which I am feeling a little bit nervous about… Santie: This is where they came through. Derek: The garage? Santie: Ja the garage, Daniel and the boy they walked in here and walked to the kitchen. Daniel gave Jerobejin a piece of bread to eat and something to drink, and that is when he broke his neck. VO: Smit then put the body in a chest freezer until the evening. Santie: There was body parts that showed that it was based in a fireplace and that is the truth and I can show you the fire place. Derek: What, put his body, or parts of his body in here? Santie: Yes Derek: Do you think Daniel is happy with us knowing about this? Santie: Daniel wants the truth to be told, because people are still looking for the body and looking for something more to bury there's nothing more. There’s nothing more. Derek: This is it. Santie: This is it. Derek: Burnt here, the rest in the drain. VO: A local municipal worker noticed Smit was tampering with the drains, the day after Jerobejin disappeared. This was peculiar behaviour as the municipality services the drains regularly. Billy: The municipal workers were busy pumping the drain when something blocked the pipe. And then they pull out, with a piece of wire, pulled out pieces of meat. It was this part, and then the hair, and a piece of one ear. VO: Billy Klaasen is a former farmworker turned activist. He started the Rural and Farmworkers' Development Organisation to help marginalised labourers. He was called in to assist when Jerobejin was reported as missing. I said, I told you guys, this is the child and then, swearing at this captain “Get up from your *ss!” and phone the people to come, and then they took over the scene again, as a crime scene. VO: DNA tests confirmed that it was Jerobejin. Smit was already detained for kidnapping and is now facing charges of Murder, Kidnapping, Assault and obstructing the ends of justice. The next court date is set for the 26th of April. Even though Triesa is still grieving, she will attend the hearing, hoping to find more answers. Triesa: I woke up last night and was about 12, then I came to sit with my child and cry by my child. Just to think how he called me, his Mom, while that man was busy with him, he called me and that's what hurts my heart so much. I was not there to help. I will never forgive him, I will never forgive him. VO: Since Jerobejin’s murder, community improvement projects have been started in an attempt to keep children off the streets. The death of Jerobejin shocked the whole town, and like Triesa, residents are desperate for answers. They have stood strong by her side from the very beginning. And as Triesa wait for the trial to commence, perhaps, now, Jerobejin is the one person that can unite the town of Klawer. 11’ South Africa is rocked by yet another alleged occult murder. This time in the small picturesque town of Klawer. We go in search of the truth 21” We enter the house of the alleged occult killer from Klawer in the Western Cape, uncovering the truth about the brutal death of a 13 year old boy. Santie: This is the Kitchen where he made him a sandwich. We uncover the disturbing details of the murder. 21” We travel to Klawer in the Western Cape and speak to the mother of murdered Jerobejin van Wyk. Tries: I want to know the whole truth. What happened to my son? What did he do to my son? What was his last words? We uncover disturbing details of yet another alleged occult killing.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): SA is gripped with yet another alleged occult murder, this time, in a small picturesque town of Klawer. Traumatised locals blame police for failing them. We visit Klawer to find the truth.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Early in February 2022, a man from a small town in the Western Cape’s Olifants Valley was arrested for the murder of 13-year-old Jerobejin van Wyk. Daniel Smit (56) has told his lawyer his actions were part of occult killings he had practiced since childhood. Smit has been charged with murder, kidnapping, assault with intent to cause grievous bodily harm, and defeating the ends of justice. But is there more to this crime?
metadata.Summary: Rumours are rife in the town as to what exactly happened when Jerobejin disappeared, Wednesday the 2nd of February. 5 children were allegedly talking to Daniel Smit, shortly before the incident. Photos have emerged of this interaction, but I am unable to prove authenticity of the photos. In the photos, Smit seems relaxed. Talking to the kids, counting down with his fingers closing in his left hand palm. As if they have had plenty of conversations with the boys before. But the situation would soon take a turn for the worse. Something happened. But what?
metadata.Further information: The kids ran away from his house. Smit got in his bakkie and followed them. In an effort to hide from Smit, one of Jerobejin’s friends hid in a dustbin, whilst Jerobejin kept running. Smit allegedly hit Jerobejin and drove over him. Breaking his neck. Smit got out, picked him up, and put him in the back of the bakkie. And drove off. This whole incident was being observed by a man filling up at a petrol station nearby, a witness. He is also willing speak to us, anonymously. He says no SAPS member approached or requested information from him, regarding that dreadful day. The witness could not believe his eyes. Jerobejin was now missing. Jerobejin’s mother, Triesa Van Wyk, went to the Klawer Police Station and two officers accompanied her to the house of Smit. “I looked him in the face and asked him where is my son, and he told me he took my child to buy him food but when he came out of the shop, he was gone.” This was a blatant lie, as Smit later admitted. Police only arrested Smit on Thursday. Police and forensics searched his property. On Friday they found body parts, stuffed in a drain outside the house. Police took DNA from Van Wyk, and is currently being analysed. We do not yet know the DNA results. Triesa, Jerobejin’s mother, however, is convinced it is her boy’s remains. “A mother just knows” a tearful Triesa told the media. It has since emerged that Smit took the body of Jerobejin, butchered it and tried to dispose of it. Allegedly, all part of an occult “sacrifice”, he told his lawyer Santie Human. She confirmed she will do an interview. Providing that it won’t interfere with the case. The Satanists’ Group has since denied that Smit is a member. Nor any affiliation. Some community members believe the murder was not an occult killing but rather racially motivated. This is the crux of the matter as the “dorpie” is very much divided at the moment. This is, unfortunately, not the first time children disappeared from this area. Over the last 3 years, 3 teenagers disappeared. Including a disabled child. With all the anger in the commity, is it reasonable for the community to want to blame Smit for these incidents too? Klawer community activist Billy Claasen, confirmed that some children were never found. He also added that this was not a crime linked to colour or race. “It is one sick White man that did this, so it could have been a sick Coloured or Black man who could have done it." Claasen is also willing to do an interview. Admitting that the tension this created, has never been experienced by the townspeople. Unfortunately, more disturbing news for Klawer. Another murder. Allegedly, racially motivated. This occurred Saturday the 12th of February. A coloured man stabbed and killed an African man. He was murdered after midnight. Unrest prevented the ambulance to get to the scene. The body was eventually removed around 06:00 in the morning. Local councilman Jan Koopman is convinced, if the police acted sooner in arresting Smit, the current situation in Klawer could have been avoided. The community is calling for Klawer SAPS Station commander, Captain Ficks, to resign. Cllr Koopman says the community lost confidence in the SAPS. A long time ago. I approached the Western Cape Police Spokesperson, Colonel André Traut, he will answer to some questions, providing I send it to him prior to filming. I will most certainly put a question to him regarding Klawer SAPS. Cllr Koopman, also acting as the spokesperson for the Van Wyk’s family, assured me that Triesa van Wyk, Jerobejin’s mother will talk to us. Van Wyk was not allowed in court when Smit appeared on Monday the 7th of February. This was despite the community protesting outside the court, to allow her access. Meanwhile, Smit stated that he will plead guilty, but even more shockingly, other murders too. Allegedly as part of the “occult”. Human, his lawyer, stated that Smit is fully co-operative. He is helping the police in finding “whatever evidence they need, where to find certain objects, like knives and tools he used to butcher the boy.” “He is divulging, whatever evidence, the investigating officers require of him.” she told me off the record. SAPS is currently investigating and looking into linking other murders to him, this in an effort to charge him once, and bring all murder charges to court. “He denies any involvement in the other missing children from Klawer” according to Human. She also added, “he is not pure evil.” Smit’s next court appearance will be 26th of April.
